 3                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

 4   Resolution Number 1193, by Senator Kennedy, 

 5   honoring the Western New York Perinatal 

 6   Bereavement Network, in conjunction with the 10th 

 7   Annual Evening to Remember on March 28, 2015.  

 8                "WHEREAS, It is the sense of this 

 9   Legislative Body to recognize and pay tribute to 

10   those women of achievement within the Empire 

11   State who have made strong contributions to their 

12   communities and who inspire others through their 

13   model citizenship; and 

14                "WHEREAS, Attendant to such concern, 

15   and in full accord with its long-standing 

16   traditions, this Legislative Body is justly proud 

17   to honor Christine Scott, Executive Director of 

18   the Western New York Perinatal Bereavement 

19   Network, in conjunction with the 10th Annual 

20   Evening to Remember on Saturday, March 28, 2015; 

21   and 

22                "WHEREAS, This auspicious event 

23   provides an opportunity for parents and families 

24   to join together in honoring their children who  

25   were lost too soon from miscarriage, ectopic 


                                                                1326

 1   pregnancy, stillbirth or early infant death; and 

 2                "WHEREAS, The Evening to Remember is 

 3   one of several events hosted by the Western 

 4   New York Perinatal Bereavement Network to bring 

 5   together those who have shared experiences and 

 6   raise public awareness; and 

 7                "WHEREAS, The ability to connect 

 8   with other grieving parents while celebrating the 

 9   memory of their children is an important part of 

10   the healing process; and 

11                "WHEREAS, Women of every race, 

12   class, and ethnic background have made invaluable 

13   contributions to the growth and strength of 

14   New York State in countless recorded and 

15   unrecorded ways; and 

16                "WHEREAS, Each year, the State of 

17   New York officially sets aside time to recognize 

18   the achievements and lives of these exemplary 

19   women, representatives of the wide-ranging and 

20   vital roles women have played in the historic 

21   development of this great Empire State and its 

22   communities; and 

23                "WHEREAS, For more than 25 years, 

24   running entirely on private donations, the 

25   Western New York Perinatal Bereavement Network 


                                                                1327

 1   has been extraordinarily dedicated to providing  

 2   educational support, community services and 

 3   referral services to families who have 

 4   experienced the loss of a child; and 

 5                "WHEREAS, Under the luminous 

 6   direction of its Executive Director, Christine 

 7   Scott, the Western New York Perinatal Bereavement 

 8   Network established the Wings of Love Memorial 

 9   Fund, which provides financial assistance to 

10   low-income families for burial and cremation 

11   expenses; the program has also created memorial 

12   gardens in several cemeteries throughout Western 

13   New York; and 

14                "WHEREAS, In addition, Christine 

15   Scott has given tirelessly of her efforts to 

16   develop and execute the Western New York 

17   Perinatal Bereavement Network's Annual Walk to 

18   Remember, which pays tribute to the approximately  

19   850,000 babies who die each year; and 

20                "WHEREAS, A professional prenatal 

21   and perinatal health educator, Christine Scott 

22   has remained steadfastly committed to educating 

23   the public and selflessly providing love and 

24   support to grieving parents and families; and 

25                "WHEREAS, Christine Scott graduated 


                                                                1328

 1   with high distinction from Genesee Community 

 2   College in 1992; she went on to earn a Bachelor  

 3   of Science degree in Health Services Management 

 4   from Indiana University in 1999; and 

 5                "WHEREAS, Rare indeed is the 

 6   impressive dedication shown by an individual for 

 7   the benefit of others which Christine Scott has 

 8   displayed throughout her life; and 

 9                "WHEREAS, This Legislative Body is 

10   pleased to have this opportunity to express its 

11   highest admiration for Christine Scott and to 

12   wish her continued success in all of her future 

13   endeavors; and 

14                "WHEREAS, It is the sense of this 

15   Legislative Body that when individuals of such 

16   noble aims and accomplishments are brought to our 

17   attention, they should be celebrated and 

18   recognized by all the citizens of the great State 

19   of New York; now, therefore, be it 

20                "RESOLVED, That this Legislative 

21   Body pause in its deliberations to honor  

22   Christine Scott, Executive Director of the 

23   Western New York Perinatal Bereavement Network, 

24   in conjunction with the 10th Annual Evening to 

25   Remember on March 28, 2015; and be it further 


                                                                1329

 1                "RESOLVED, That a copy of this 

 2   resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted to 

 3   Christine Scott."

 4                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

 5   Kennedy.

 6                SENATOR KENNEDY:   Thank you, 

 7   Mr. President.

 8                It is an extreme honor for me to 

 9   stand here in this chamber to honor a woman who 

10   has honored so many families, thousands of 

11   families in Western New York and across the 

12   state, and who is present here with us them 

13   morning, Christine Scott.  

14                Christine is joined by her sister 

15   Cathy Payne, who came in from Buffalo, the two of 

16   them came in from Buffalo last night to join us 

17   for this occasion.  

18                We're doing a couple of things by 

19   this resolution.  We are recognizing the Western 

20   New York Perinatal Bereavement Network for their 

21   25 years of service to families that have lost a 

22   child, either newborn, infant or in utero, and 

23   have had that pain that they've lived with.  And 

24   the Western New York Perinatal Bereavement 

25   Network for 25 years has been with them to help 


                                                                1330

 1   them through those very difficult times.

 2                The 28th of this month, the Western 

 3   New York Perinatal Bereavement Network will host 

 4   its Evening to Remember, where families gather 

 5   together to not only share stories and to help 

 6   each other through their difficult times, but to 

 7   remember the loved ones that they have lost, at 

 8   the same time raising funds for the programs that 

 9   help families as they experience this difficult 

10   and tragic loss in their lives.

11                Christine Scott is the executive 

12   director of that incredible organization and has 

13   been on the front lines of helping families, 

14   helping mothers and fathers, aunts and uncles, 

15   brothers and sisters that lose a loved one, lose 

16   a newborn, lose a child.  She has done this, her 

17   driving force has been a loss in her own life 

18   back on May 27, 2000.  Jacob Wesley Scott came 

19   into our lives, came into Christine Scott's life 

20   and was lost, stillbirth, and has driven 

21   Christine Scott to help other people in the most 

22   difficult, transformative, heartbreaking times in 

23   their lives.  

24                And with an incredible amount of 

25   dignity and class and drive and passion, she has 


                                                                1331

 1   taken this loss that she and her family 

 2   experienced and has transformed it into helping 

 3   families across Western New York and across this 

 4   state.

 5                Not only when people lose a child 

 6   has she been there, but she's also been there 

 7   from a legislative capacity, when we passed the 

 8   bill that recognized the children that were lost 

 9   to stillbirth that allowed thousands and 

10   thousands of families, tens of thousands of 

11   families that have lost a child through 

12   stillbirth, because of legislation that we passed 

13   in this chamber a couple of years ago, families 

14   have been able to get a birth certificate 

15   recognizing that their child existed.  

16                Previous to that legislation that 

17   Christine and her organization and other 

18   organizations across the state championed, 

19   families were only given a death certificate, 

20   that only added to the pain that they went 

21   through that their child never actually existed.

22                We owe Christine not just this 

23   honor, but we owe Christine a debt of gratitude 

24   from Western New York that we will never be able 

25   to repay.  But I know the driving force behind 


                                                                1332

 1   Christine is Jacob and the Wings of Love 

 2   organization that is inspired by Jacob and that 

 3   proudly is recognized by a monarch butterfly -- 

 4   that I recognized Christine and her sister both 

 5   wear on their lapels today -- and is a sign that 

 6   Jacob is with Christine, her family, and with all 

 7   of us and is the symbol behind the Wings of Love.  

 8                And this organization helps families 

 9   that cannot afford to bury their lost child with 

10   dignity, the ability to do that.

11                Thank you, Christine Scott, for 

12   everything you do for all of us.  Thank you for 

13   what you've done for thousands of families across 

14   this state, what you continue to do.  

15   Congratulations to the Wings of Love and the 

16   wonderful, wonderful organization that you've 

17   established, as well as the Western New York 

18   Perinatal Bereavement Network and the thousands 

19   of parents that you have touched, the 

20   organization has touched and continues to touch 

21   every single day, including today -- including 

22   today -- when privately, before we met here in 

23   this chamber, Christine went and met with a young 

24   man, Gary Ginsburg, who lost Emma Olivia Ginsburg 

25   just a couple of weeks ago.  


                                                                1333

 1                He's the deputy director of media 

 2   relations in the Senate.  And Christine was kind 

 3   enough to share her passion for helping people 

 4   with someone close to all of us.

 5                So again, thank you for what you do 

 6   every day, and it is an honor to stand here to 

 7   honor you.  Congratulations.

25   Mr. President.


                                                                1337

 1                I rise on behalf of the thousands of 

 2   members in dozens of Vietnam Veterans of America 

 3   posts here in the great State of New York.

 4                This Sunday, March 29th, is Vietnam 

 5   Veterans Day.  The Vietnam War was an extremely 

 6   divisive issue among the people of the United 

 7   States, and it caused a generation of veterans to 

 8   wait way far too long for our country to 

 9   acknowledge and honor their efforts and their 

10   sacrifice.

11                My uncle Peter, who saw four tours 

12   in Vietnam and adopted a little Vietnamese girl 

13   out of the orphanage, I stand here proudly to 

14   tell you he is a hero to me.

15                Today's legislation declares the 

16   Vietnam Veterans of America to be recognized as a 

17   benevolent order right here in New York.  Is just 

18   as much for my uncle Peter as it is for the 

19   thousands of Vietnam veterans living in our 

20   state.

21                For those of you who don't know, the 

22   Vietnam Veterans of America's goals are to 

23   promote and support the full range of issues 

24   important to Vietnam veterans.  It is to create a 

25   new identity for this generation of veterans and 


                                                                1338

 1   to change the public perception of the Vietnam 

 2   veterans.

 3                By voting in favor of this 

 4   legislation, we once again send a clear message 

 5   to those who served our nation during this time.  

 6   Mission accomplished, and welcome home.

 7                Thank you, Mr. President.

 8                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

 9   Murphy to be recorded in the affirmative.

10                Senator Croci to explain his vote.

14   colleague Senator Murphy for bringing this 

15   important legislation to the floor and compliment 

16   this chamber for the work that we have done in 

17   welcoming home veterans who did not receive a 

18   welcome home when they got off the plane so many 

19   years ago.  

20                It's been a process that this 

21   country has gone through, and certainly the State 

22   of New York has been a leader in recognizing how 

23   important their service and their sacrifice -- 

24   and that of their families -- has been to this 

25   country.  


                                                                1339

 1                The Vietnam Veterans of America, a 

 2   wonderful organization that not only helps in the 

 3   issues that affect the Vietnam veterans, but 

 4   through their other charitable works, including 

 5   their thrift stores, helps people in low-income

 8   country.  

 9                So, Senator Murphy and to all my 

10   colleagues who support this legislation, thank 

11   you for what you're doing in welcoming home our 

12   heroes.
